title: Roast Chicken
subtitle: Classic butter-roasted whole chicken
excerpt: A whole chicken rubbed with butter and herbs, roasted at high heat until the skin is golden and crisp and the meat is juicy throughout. The most fundamental and satisfying thing a home cook can make; everything else follows from getting this right.

recipe.sourceNotes: Roast chicken is the foundational recipe of British, French, and American home cooking, and many celebrated chefs have identified it as the dish they would judge a cook's skill by. The French term for roast chicken is poulet rôti, and it occupies a central place in French bourgeois cooking as the Sunday lunch. The technique is simple: the chicken is buttered, seasoned, and roasted at sufficient heat that the skin crisps and colours while the breast and thigh cook through. The difficulty is achieving both simultaneously: breast meat is cooked at 71°C while thigh meat benefits from reaching 74 to 75°C. Starting the chicken on its side, turning it, and finishing breast-up is one approach; others roast breast-down and finish breast-up. The critical technique that is universally agreed upon is resting the bird after roasting for at least 15 minutes.

recipeTools.notes: Check the thigh meat between the leg and body. At 74°C the bird is done.

content.text: Take the chicken out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking. Cold chicken going into a hot oven means the outside is done before the inside is safe. Rest the bird for at least 15 minutes after roasting, covered loosely with foil; the internal temperature rises a further 3 to 4 degrees during resting and the juices redistribute through the meat.

items.preparation: a good free-range bird; brought to room temperature 1 hour before cooking
halved; one half inside the cavity
unpeeled; stuffed inside the cavity with the lemon

content.text: Heat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Mix the softened butter with the thyme, salt, and pepper. Pat the chicken dry with kitchen paper. Rub the butter mixture all over the outside of the bird and push a little under the skin of the breast. Put the lemon half and garlic cloves inside the cavity. Place the onion halves in a roasting tin and sit the chicken on top.

Roast for 20 minutes at the high heat to colour the skin. Reduce to 190°C / fan 170°C / gas 5. Continue roasting for 45 to 55 minutes, basting once or twice with the pan juices. A 1.8 kg chicken takes about 70 to 75 minutes total. Test by piercing the thickest part of the thigh: the juices should run completely clear with no trace of pink.

Transfer to a board and rest, loosely covered, for 15 to 20 minutes. Use the resting juices and any pan juices to make a quick gravy by heating them in the roasting tin on the hob with a splash of wine or stock. Carve at the table.
